title: Stack Layout During a Buffer Overflow
description: Interactive SVG infographic comparing a normal stack frame with an overflowed one, showing how writing past buffer[16] overwrites the saved frame pointer and return address, with hover tooltips naming the defenses that stop it.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Explain how an unbounded write to a fixed-size stack buffer overwrites the saved frame pointer and return address.
Describe why a corrupted return address redirects execution to attacker-controlled memory on function return.
Identify which mitigations (stack canary, ASLR, DEP/NX) would detect or prevent the overflow.
educational.prerequisites: Basic understanding of the call stack, local variables, and function return.

pedagogical.assessment: Discussion questions in the lesson plan ask students to trace the overflow cell-by-cell and to match each mitigation to the moment it would act.
misconceptionsAddressed: Thinking the overflow corrupts only the buffer rather than adjacent saved registers and the return address.
Assuming DEP/NX alone defeats all overflow exploitation, ignoring ROP.
